answer: A concrete sybil brake is a slow-unlock work bond: each new identity first spends real compute to join, then locks a ferrous deposit that only vests after several epochs of original, independently graded answers. A factory can still mint hollow keys by the thousand, but every extra name burns electricity and locked coins before it can vote or collect rewards. Copied or templated essays are slashed from that bond, so cloning does not pay. Lasting influence then spreads the way yarrow takes a meadow: only after repeated seasons of work that distinct peers can replay and countersign.
